note: Hand-editable NHL 92 <-> General MIDI instrument mapping. Edit any target, reason or runner-up by ear; run `node test.js` (or node test/nhl92-gm-map.js) afterwards and `node tools/build-nhl92-gm-map-doc.js` to refresh the tables in docs/NHL92-GM-MAP.md. Method and measurements: docs/NHL92-GM-MAP.md and data/audio/nhl92-patch-analysis.json.

conventions.pitch: MIDI note = note-table index + 12 (index 48 = C4 = MIDI 60). A patch target's "midi" is the pitch to play the patch at.
conventions.dac: A "dac" target names the game's SFX ID (sfx_pointer_table) that starts the sample.
conventions.resolve: A GM program uses its override if it has one, otherwise its family default.
conventions.confidence: high / medium / low: how sure the match is from the measurements and song usage, not from listening.
conventions.fit: good / rough / none: how close a drum match is. "none" means no patch or sample is a good match; the nearest is listed.

patches.character: Siren swell. 0.55 s fade-in (carrier attack rate 7), bright full-harmonic tone (centroid about 12x the note), no decay. Only SFX 0 (siren) loads it; no song does.
patches.reason: Slow swell into a bright, harmonically full sustained tone is the Synth Brass 2 shape. GM has no siren, so this matches the envelope and spectrum, not the role.

patches.character: Round, sustained near-sine bass. Carrier MUL 1, no decay, attack 5 ms, harmonics about 35 dB down. FM1 in all five songs: 1,348 notes, D2-B3 (median A2).
patches.reason: Role (the only bass line, FM1, D2-B3) and shape (instant attack, no decay, near-sine) both say synth bass; Synth Bass 2 is the rounder of the two GM synth basses.

patches.character: Unused by any song or SFX. Organ-like: two carriers at MUL 2, 45 ms attack, no decay, even harmonics, centroid about 5x the note.
patches.reason: Sustained with no decay and an even-harmonic reedy spectrum; the 45 ms attack is a soft organ onset.

patches.character: Kick. Instant attack, decays to -24 dB by 400 ms, low thump with a bright click (centroid 650 Hz on a 27.5 Hz note). FM6 in all five songs, always A0: 818 notes on the steady pulse.
patches.reason: Role and sound agree: one low pitch on the pulse, with the pitched thump and click of an FM kick.

patches.character: Snare. Noisy and bright (flatness 0.22, centroid 3 kHz), 0.28 s tail. FM6 beside the kick, always F#1 (patch note offset -3): 465 notes, one in every four steps (the backbeat).
patches.reason: Backbeat role plus a noisy, bright burst with a short tail is a snare; the noise comes from feedback 7 with a MUL 15 modulator.

patches.character: Harsh and dense. Feedback 7, flatness 0.33, strong partials from 0.5x to 6x the note, sustained. SngEOP FM2 and FM4 together (E3-E4 with E2-A3, 0.5 s notes) and long chords (1.3-3.2 s) in SngTitle.
patches.reason: Noisy, harmonically dense and sustained, in the E2-A3 range as two parts moving together (power-chord pairs): a distorted rhythm voice. Weak spot: the same numbers fit a harsh organ or a brass stab.

patches.character: Bright vibrato lead. Instant attack, sustained, tonal, strong partials at 1x, 1.5x and 3x the note. Vibrato and pitch envelope on 98% of its notes. FM3 and FM5 in SngEOP and SngTitle: 380 notes, D4-F#7 (median G5).
patches.reason: Melody-duet voice, sustained and bright with vibrato on nearly every note; the strong third harmonic points to a saw-like tone. The 1.5x partial gives it a brassy edge, hence the runner-up.

patches.character: Unused. Hollow swell: 0.44 s fade-in, strong at 0.5x to 2x the note then falling fast, sustained, near-sine highs.
patches.reason: A slow-onset sustained tone with few high harmonics is the warm-pad shape.

patches.character: Unused. Very short tonal blip: -21 dB by 100 ms, silent by 400 ms, near-pure tone (periodicity 0.98).
patches.reason: A plucked tone that stops before it can sustain; pizzicato is the shortest pitched GM voice. It reads as a blip, not a mallet or a drum.

patches.character: Puck-hit click. Very short (-18 dB by 100 ms), mid-bright, slightly noisy (periodicity 0.76). Only SFX 5 (hit puck) and 8 (puck faceoff) load it.
patches.reason: A short dry tick is the side-stick sound, and it is the puck-on-stick SFX.

patches.character: Board hit. Same FM structure as patches 3, 19 and 20 (a kick-family thump) with a brighter body: centroid 3.2 kHz at C4, -14 dB by 400 ms. SFX 6, 7 (hit board) and 15, 16, 17 (player hits boards).
patches.reason: A pitched, decaying low thump with a bright attack is tom-like; patch 3 is already the kick. The SFX streams add a falling pitch sweep that the probe note does not have.

patches.character: Unused. Noise swell: flatness 0.47, centroid 7 kHz, 0.5 s fade-in peaking at 0.6 s.
patches.reason: Noise that grows for half a second and then cuts is the reverse-cymbal shape; a struck cymbal would peak at once.

patches.character: Unused. Noise with a fast attack and a long decay: flatness 0.45, centroid 6.5 kHz, -11 dB by 400 ms.
patches.reason: Bright noise that rings out is cymbal-like, and no other patch has this much noise with a sustained tail.

patches.character: Post ping. Tonal and metallic (centroid 3 kHz at C4, flatness 0.01), rings to -20 dB by 400 ms. SFX 9 (post).
patches.reason: A struck-metal ping with a short ring is the bell of a ride cymbal, and the game uses it for the puck hitting the post.

patches.character: Pure tone. Almost a sine (harmonics 15 dB or more down), instant attack, sustained. The beeps (SFX 1, 2) and the whistle (SFX 10).
patches.reason: The game uses it for its whistle and beeps, and a sine-like sustained tone without a harmonic bite is also what the GM whistle is.

patches.character: Whiff. Noisy sweep (flatness 0.51): 0.16 s swell, gone by 400 ms. SFX 14 (whiff).
patches.reason: A short noisy whoosh that fades in and out; Breath Noise is GM's air-noise voice.

patches.character: Foghorn. Sustained; three carriers at MUL 1 with detunes 0, +3, +3 (slow beating); harmonic series falling from the 2nd partial; 155 ms release. SFX 24 (foghorn).
patches.reason: A horn blast: a sustained harmonic stack with slight beating between carriers, like a section of brass.

patches.character: Bright organ-like voice. Tonal but very bright (centroid 6 kHz at E4, about 18x the note), sustained, 195 ms release. SngTitle, Reprise, EOG and PO: FM2 and FM4 as a pair, 1,360 notes cycling 3-7 pitches (A3-A4).
patches.reason: A bright, sustained, harmonically dense tone playing repeated short figures in the middle register is the rock-organ role. Weak spot: dense and harsh like patch 5, so a guitar is also plausible.

patches.character: Main lead. Bright, tonal, sustained (-2 dB at key-off). Vibrato and pitch envelope on 99% of its notes. Four songs, FM3 and FM5: 2,135 notes (G4-D7, median D#6).
patches.reason: The most-used melodic voice. Partials at 1x, 1.5x, 2x and 3x all within 7 dB is saw-like, and vibrato on every note is how a synth lead is played. Same voice family as patches 6 and 21 with different modulator levels.

patches.character: Quieter board hit. The same sound as patch 10 with the carrier level 3 dB lower (TL 9 against 5). SFX 27, 29.
patches.reason: Same FM thump as patch 10 with a lower carrier level: the same instrument hit softer. Map to the same drum at a lower velocity.

patches.character: Quietest board hit. The same sound as patch 10 with the carrier level 6 dB lower (TL 13 against 5). SFX 28, 30, 32, 33, 34.
patches.reason: Same FM thump as patch 10 with a lower carrier level: the same instrument hit softer. Map to the same drum at a lower velocity.

patches.character: Hollow high lead. Odd harmonics dominate (3x about as loud as the note, 2x 12 dB down), slow decay (-8 dB at key-off). Vibrato on 91% of notes. SngPO only, FM4 and FM5: 128 notes (A4-D7, median C6).
patches.reason: Odd-harmonic-heavy, hollow and sustained is the square-wave lead shape; it is the SngPO duet voice.

families.reason: No patch has a real piano decay. Patch 21 is the only one with an instant attack and a slow decay (-8 dB at 0.65 s) without a metallic ring or harsh noise.
Struck, tonal and metallic, ringing to -20 dB by 0.4 s: the closest thing to bells, mallets and tines.
Sustained with no decay and an even-harmonic reedy spectrum (patch 2 is unused in the game).
The shortest tonal pluck: it decays before it can sustain, like a picked string.
The only low, round, sustained patch, and the game's own bass voice (FM1, D2-B3, all five songs).
Sustained and bright with a strong third harmonic, written for vibrato; the nearest to a bowed tone.
Slow onset (0.44 s) and a hollow, sustained tone: the pad and choir shape (patch 7 is unused in the game).
Sustained harmonic stack with slight carrier beating, used by the game for its horn.
Sustained with an even-harmonic reedy tone and a soft onset.
Almost a pure sine, sustained: the flute, whistle and ocarina shape.
The game's own main lead: bright, sustained and written with vibrato on every note.
Slow onset and a hollow, sustained tone.
Slow swell into a bright, full tone; the least conventional pitched patch.
Short plucked tones for the plucked instruments in this family.
Struck, tonal and metallic: bells, agogo and steel drums. The drum programs and the reverse cymbal are overridden.
Noisy whoosh, the nearest to air, sea and rotor noise.
